title: A Phone Call About the Prophet's Mercy in Mecca
script: Amir: [excited] Laila, I just finished reading about the conquest of Mecca. I couldn't stop thinking about it, so I called you.
Laila: [curious] Oh, tell me. Which part stood out to you the most?
Amir: [thoughtful] The part where Prophet Muhammad finally returned to Mecca, after years of being forced to leave and being persecuted there.
Laila: [reflective] Right, the same people who had hurt him and his followers for years.
Amir: [with feeling] Exactly. And when he entered the city with his army, everyone expected punishment, maybe even revenge.
Laila: [curious] What did he do instead?
Amir: [warmly] He asked the people gathered there, what do you expect me to do with you now?
Laila: [thoughtful] That's a heavy question after everything they had done to him.
Amir: [softly] They said, we expect goodness from you, brother and son of a noble brother.
Laila: [curious] And how did he respond to that?
Amir: [with emotion] He said, go, for you are free. No blame will be on you today.
Laila: [amazed] After everything, he chose complete forgiveness, at the height of his own power.
Amir: [thoughtful] That's what struck me most. He had every reason and every ability to punish them, and he simply forgave.
Laila: [gently] It reminds me of Yusuf forgiving his brothers, almost the exact same words, actually.
Amir: [warmly] I noticed that too. Real mercy shows itself clearest when someone finally holds power over those who wronged them.
Laila: [reflective] It makes me think about grudges I still carry over much smaller things, honestly.
Amir: [gently] Same here. If he could forgive an entire city, I think I can let go of my smaller frustrations too.
Laila: [warmly] Thank you for calling and sharing this. I needed this reminder tonight, more than you know.

quiz.question: What event was Amir reading about when he called Laila?
quiz.explanation: Amir explains he was reading about the conquest of Mecca.

quiz.question: What did people expect when Prophet Muhammad entered Mecca with his army?
quiz.explanation: Everyone expected punishment, maybe even revenge, given the years of persecution.

quiz.question: What did the Prophet ask the people gathered in Mecca?
options: What do you expect me to do with you now?
Why they stayed in the city
quiz.explanation: He asked them what they expected him to do with them now.

quiz.question: What did the Prophet say to the people of Mecca?
options: Go, for you are free, no blame will be on you today
You must leave the city forever
quiz.explanation: He told them, go, for you are free, no blame will be on you today.

quiz.question: What connection does Laila notice in the conversation?
options: A connection to a different religion entirely
That his words echo Yusuf forgiving his brothers
That the story has no historical basis
That mercy was never mentioned before
quiz.explanation: Laila notices the Prophet's words echo Yusuf forgiving his brothers, almost the exact same phrasing.
